text:
ryan: Quick FYI — I opened a PR to change the async job endpoint behavior for long-running tasks. Main goals: introduce a short-lived polling_token (vs using opaque request_id for polling), make cancel idempotent and async, and add explicit `expires_at` to the status payload. Please skim and flag blockers. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/async-api/pulls/142

alex: Reading. Quick Q: why a separate polling_token? can we not reuse request_id?

ryan: Short answer: request_id stays as an audit key (global), but we want a lighter token for polling that can be rotated/expired without invalidating historical logs. polling_token is also scoped to the worker region which lets us route cheaper.

maria: Sounds ok. Does this break existing SDKs that call GET /jobs/:request_id/status?

ryan: Backcompat plan: GET /jobs/:request_id/status will continue to work for now and will return the new schema (with `polling_token` in the response). Clients that rely on the old shape must be updated within 2 releases. We'll add a compat header `X-Job-Schema: v1` during deprecation window.

sam: What about cancel semantics? If we return 202 for cancel and actual cancellation is async, do we surface intermediate states? e.g., CANCELLING -> CANCELLED or still RUNNING?

r yan: We propose status transitions: PENDING -> RUNNING -> CANCELLING -> CANCELLED/FAILED/SUCCEEDED. When you POST /jobs/:request_id/cancel we return 202 + body {"status":"CANCELLING","polling_token":"...","eta_seconds":30}. After cancellation completes, normal status polling will show CANCELLED.

alex: Need to call out idempotency: repeated cancels should return idempotent 202 with current cancellation state. Also what about timeouts? server-side should have a max ttl per job and send `expires_at` in ISO8601. Clients should stop polling after that.

ryan: Agreed. PR includes these lines. Sample response in the thread for quick copy:```json
{
  "request_id": "req_01FZ...",
  "polling_token": "pt_7a9...",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "progress": {"percent": 0},
  "eta_seconds": null,
  "expires_at": "2026-10-01T12:34:56Z",
  "links": {"cancel": "/jobs/req_01FZ/cancel"}
}
```

maria: Thanks — we should include `schema_version` and `deprecated_fields` array so clients can programmatically detect changes.

sam: Also suggest a small grace_window after cancel (10s) to flush KV cache and free resources, but keep reporting state= CANCELLING.

ryan: Adding `grace_window_seconds` to the cancel response is reasonable. I'll update the PR and add a unit/integration test for a cancel race (cancel while RUNNING -> ensure final state CANCELLED and no double-charges).

alex: Ping me on the PR once tests pass. Also include a sample curl snippet for SDK folks:```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/jobs/req_01FZ/cancel
```

maria: Logistics — when do we want to roll this to prod? We need SDK patches and a short deprecation notice.

ryan: Proposed rollout: feature flag on Monday 2026-03-23, start sending `X-Job-Schema: v1` for flagged traffic for 1 week, then flip for all. Deprecation notice to customers in two weeks.

sam: Oncall — @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary at 09:30 PT on rollout day?

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled for 2026-03-23 09:30 PT — watchlist: job-frontend, job-worker-us-east. Notifications will post to #incidents if error rate > 0.5%.

alex: Great. I left a couple of inline comments about error codes and a11y of error messages. Quick thumbs if no more blockers and we can merge after tests. :thumbsup:

ryan: Thanks all — merging once CI is green and tests added. Will post final rollout checklist here.
